papers.award: Best Thesis Award · UNC Department of Public Policy
papers.title: Movement-Mediated Vertical Policy Feedback
papers.body: How can local governments advance climate policy at higher levels? Drawing on 41 interviews with organizers and officials in Austin, Charlotte and Portland, I argue that cities do it, often without meaning to, by resourcing and channeling social movements.
papers.advisors: Advisors: Dr. Angel Hsu and Dr. Elizabeth Korver-Glenn

papers.title: Leaderless But Not Powerless
papers.body: Why did Nepal’s Discord-organized Gen Z uprising produce lasting electoral change when peer movements collapsed? Built on interviews with 23 activists and five politicians during an independent study in Kathmandu, supported by the Morehead-Cain Lovelace Fund for Discovery.

course.tag: A course I designed and taught · Spring 2026
course.title: Resistance to Authoritarianism
course.body: Through UNC’s Carolina Student Training and Research program (C-START), I taught my peers a one-credit course I built from my own research. After trips to Chile, Uruguay, Peru and Mexico, I designed a semester of weekly two-hour seminars on how movements have resisted and outlasted authoritarian rule, using primary sources, documentary film and guest speakers, and asked what they can teach us about defending democratic institutions.
course.advisors: Mentors: Professor Gabrielle Calvocoressi and Dr. Evelyne Huber

items.title: Design Thinking for the Public Good
items.text: Ran listening sessions and mapped the ecosystem around the Durham Arts Council to find out why many residents don’t realize it’s free and open to all.

items.title: Justice in Public Policy
items.text: An honors seminar applying moral philosophy to live policy debates, with weekly essays weighing utilitarian, deontological and paternalism arguments on cases from the Chevron ruling to social media rules for children.

items.title: Political Parties
items.text: Graduate seminar on how parties organize democratic politics and how party systems change. My final paper designs a study of when networked protest movements reshape party systems, building on my Nepal fieldwork.

items.title: Courageous Conversations: Israel & Palestine
items.text: A course built around dialogue across deep disagreement, using the Israel–Palestine conflict as its case.

items.title: Quantitative Analysis & Research Design
items.text: Stata, R and the habit of asking “compared to what?”

items.label: Idaho Climate Conversations, 2023
items.tip_text: With a friend, I drove a Prius through all 44 Idaho counties in two weeks and recorded around 130 conversations with residents about the climate changes they were seeing. Funded by a community GoFundMe. Mentor: Dr. Aly Bean. Click to watch.

items.label: Meridian housing study, 2023
items.tip_text: With three Boise State classmates, I studied housing affordability for the Meridian City Council and recommended rental assistance, subsidies for affordable housing, and rezoning near the freeway. Mentors: Dr. Vanessa Fry and Dr. Krista Paulsen. Click to read the coverage.
